claims.claim: Python's bool type has exactly two constant instances, True and False.
An object is normally truthy unless __bool__ returns False or __len__ returns zero; built-in falsey examples include None, numeric zero, and empty collections.
bool is a subclass of int, and False/True behave as 0/1 in many numeric contexts; the documentation discourages relying on that behavior.
x or y returns x when x is true and otherwise y; x and y returns x when x is false and otherwise y.
or evaluates its second operand only when the first is false, while and evaluates its second operand only when the first is true.
not performs truth testing and returns True or False.
